chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i from Zurara who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Should I marry a Murji'a or a Haruriyya? He said: 'There is no harm for you in marrying the simple-minded (or: the ordinary) among the women.'
Zurara said: I said: 'By Allah, she is merely a believer or a disbeliever.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And where are the people of Thaniyat Allah?'
The word of Allah is truer than your word: 'Except for the weak among men and women and children who cannot devise a way nor are they guided to a way.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ ثَنْوَى اَللَّهِ: The people of 'God's Thaniya' (a reference to a specific Quranic verse or concept of weakness/exemption)
key_terms.الْبُلْهِ: The simple-minded or ordinary (in religious rigor)
key_terms.اَلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: The weak/exempted (those excused from full religious obligation)
key_terms.حَرُورِيَّةً: A female adherent of the Haruriyya sect
key_terms.مُرْجِئَةً: A female adherent of the Murji'a sect

ai.seo_question: Can a Shia Muslim marry a woman from the Murji'a or Haruriyya sects?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permits marriage to women from the Murji'a and Haruriyya sects, classifying them as 'simple-minded' (al-bulh) rather than outright disbelievers, thereby avoiding the strict ruling of *kufr* for their basic faith. He supports this nuanced view by citing Quran 4:98 regarding the 'weak' who are excused from full accountability, a principle central to Shia *fiqh al-ahwal* (personal status law) in distinguishing between theological deviation and ritual invalidity. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of pragmatic categorization, where sectarian affiliation does not automatically preclude marital validity if the individual maintains core Islamic tenets.
